Text.Text: The circuit's quiet. I'm still getting used to it. If you want to work on Red Bloom, find me here. We can keep the rules closer than the blades this time.
You're quick with those blades. Bring your Twin Blade training to rank 50, then we can speak of the rest. Speed was the easy part for me, too.

They still use my name to sell fights in the club backrooms. Six Red Bloom adepts are performing a form I taught them without its restraint. Defeat the six and bring me their bout ledger. I'd like to know who paid to watch that lesson discarded.
Take this key into the fight club and find the backrooms entrance. They won't know your name there. I hope you'll leave it that way.
Two cuts. They open together, or they're just cuts. Most people spend a career teaching two blades to agree. The bloom is what happens after they stop needing to. That's all I'll say standing up.

Mine, once removed. Someone in the backrooms taught my form from watching my old bouts. Kept the shape. Dropped the rules. The rules were the part that cost me something. Six students so far. There will be sixty if the school stays open.
Names. Odds. Which bouts were fixed to end in a funeral. I left the circuit so my form would stop filling graves. The ledger will tell me how far behind I already am.
Six adepts in the fight club backrooms. Bring their ledger here to the casino. I'll read the names myself.
You're moving differently. Slower. Good -- that's the weight of doing it right. The ledger.
Thirty-one bouts. Nine marked to end wrong. You stopped six students; the school barely noticed. It will. Take your pay. Come back when your cuts have settled.

Five specialists have fitted the backroom pits with shock gear. A fighter who falls gets hurt for the crowd a second time. Beat the five and bring me their regulator. There was a time I thought winning there meant something.
Bring the regulator here. I want it away from any ring that still has a fighter in it.
Like me, if you'd only ever seen me angry. They'll pair on you -- one high, one low, both patient. Don't watch the blades. Watch the feet. And never let two of them agree on a rhythm.

That regulator hung over my last title bout. It cut the current the instant I dropped my opponent -- saved her life. Someone rewired mercy into a goad. I'd like it back on my wall, ugly and honest. That's all.
A bout I won. The crowd wanted the second cut. I gave it. She was nineteen. That's the whole story anyone is owed, including you. My rules exist so it stays the only one.
Five specialists in the backrooms have the shock regulator. Beat them and bring it here.
Burns on your knuckles. You pulled it live. The regulator, then.

They soldered the mercy out of it. Cheap work. I'll rebuild it the way it hung in my day. You've cut the school's teachers out from under it -- which means the man at the deep gate knows your name now. Before you go near him, we talk. That's not a request.

The warden will answer a challenge in the backrooms. I know him well enough to be sure of that. Defeat him and bring me his pit sigil. Take someone beside you. He was very good at finding the moment a fighter thought the danger had passed.
Use the backrooms challenge marker to call him. He'll consider it a courtesy. When he's beaten, bring me the sigil. He'd rather it went to someone who earned it through him.

I broke his sigil with the last clean bloom I ever threw. He bowed. The crowd never understood that bow. He didn't keep the broken sigil out of shame -- he kept it as a promise that no one would pass him carelessly again. When you knock, he'll already know whose student you are.

Because he'd let me pass. Whatever's left of that circuit still bows to me, and a door that opens for your name proves nothing and fixes less. It has to be someone the backrooms owe nothing. And if I went down those stairs, I'm not sure which of us I'd be by the bottom.
He learns a lone fighter's rhythm quickly. Company gives him more to read. I still count the names of challengers who went in proud; I'd rather you gave him a harder fight than that.
Call the warden at the backrooms challenge marker. Beat him and return his pit sigil.
I felt it from up here. Don't ask me how. Let me see the sigil.

Both cracks are mine, in a way. He was the best thing about that circuit and the last of my era standing. Take your pay and rest. The promoters still in the backrooms fight for something less complicated: their purses.

Four promoters still hold the circuit's payout chit. They've made a living selling what we did to one another. Defeat the four in the backrooms and bring it here. I'm ready to see the accounts closed.
Collect the chit from the promoters. Don't let them put your name on another purse.

A patient counter-fighter, a pair who share a tempo, and a big one who thinks pain makes him rich. Watch the pair; don't stand between them. If you've brought help, keep close enough to cover whoever they choose first.

My title. Someone is wearing it. She took my name off the boards and put the bloom back to work in the deep pit, the way the crowd always wanted it from me. I'm told she throws it red every night. Ask me the rest when the circle's dead. I'll answer. I keep my word slowly, but I keep it.

It goes to people on this moon who set odds and hate being lied to, with my statement attached. The backrooms exist because the money is invisible. The promoter's own hand makes it visible. I don't need him dead. I need him poor, and famous for the right things. Poor men can't rent pits.
The four promoters in the backrooms have the payout chit. Bring it here when their circuit is finished.
You're not bleeding. They were the promoter's best and you're not bleeding. Show me the chit.

Good ink. Heavy hand. Frightened man. This closes every account but one -- the room where my title lives. Sit down before you ask. When you're ready to hear about her, I'll tell you all of it, and then you'll wish I hadn't.

The master is in the Private Pit. Call her at the challenge marker and defeat her. You know the form now; don't let knowing it make you careless. Come back to the casino afterward. I want to see you walk out of this school.
She'll answer the Private Pit's challenge marker. Keep your distance when the first cut comes, and don't mistake the pause for the end. Come back here when she's beaten.

Watch the second cut. She makes it follow the first so neatly that people answer one and forget the other. If you've brought help, cover whoever takes that first exchange. Alone, keep enough guard to answer both. Don't race her simply because she invites you to.

The best I ever trained, and the only one I ever refused to pass. She asked what I was willing to bleed, the day we met. Same thing I asked you. Her answer was everyone else. I should have ended it there. I gave her footwork instead. This is me paying that debt with your hands, and I know exactly what that makes me.

Then the form has no owner left but the two of us, and I'm retired. The rules come with it, whether you want them or not. You've been keeping them for five bouts already, mostly without noticing. That was the real trial. Her ring is just the last question on it.
The Private Pit has the master's challenge marker. Beat her, then come back to the casino. Leave the crowd to itself.
The backrooms went quiet an hour ago. Real quiet, not held-breath quiet. Say it anyway. I want to hear it in a living voice.
You walked back out. I'm glad. Your pay is here, and I'm willing to teach you Red Bloom if you still want it. We won't need a crowd for that. Just enough room to learn when the blades should stop.
Let me ask something else.
Whatever it costs. I'm in.
What is the Red Bloom?
Whose students are they?
What do you want with their ledger?
I don't have an answer yet.
Here. The whole book.
One more question.
Five, and the regulator. Done.
How will the specialists come at me?
Why does the regulator matter to you?
Why did you leave the circuit?
Not yet.
Off the wall. It's yours.
Back to the gate.
I'll face him. You have my word.
You know him?
Why not go yourself?
What difference will company make?
I need to find people I trust.
It's done. Here's his sigil.
Go back over the four.
Four. And I'll bring you his ink.
What should I know about the four?
Who's in the champion's room?
What happens to the chit after?
Soon. Not tonight.
The chit. His signature is on everything.
Go over it again.
I'll challenge her.
How do I beat her form?
What was she to you?
And when it's over -- what then?
I need time to get ready.
She's dead. The bloom is finished.
